speaker: Doctor
text:
Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned a chronic cough and recurrent bronchitis; how many times per year have you experienced these episodes, and do you notice any specific triggers like cold air, dust, or exercise?

REQUEST TEST: Spirometry (PFTs) with bronchodilator response.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Spirometry (PFTs) with bronchodilator response shows Reduced FVC, Reduced FEV1, and a Normal FEV1/FVC Ratio.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The spirometry shows a restrictive pattern (reduced FVC and FEV1 with a normal ratio), which is unusual for typical chronic bronchitis; do you have a history of lung fibrosis, connective tissue disease, or recent exposure to toxins or asbestos?

REQUEST TEST: High-Resolution CT (HRCT) of the Chest.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: High-Resolution CT (HRCT) of the Chest shows irregular opacities in the right middle lobe and diffuse airway thickening.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The HRCT confirms a restrictive pattern with airway thickening and focal opacities; does the chronic cough worsen significantly in the morning or at night, and do you experience shortness of breath or wheezing during these episodes?

REQUEST IMAGES: Chest CT follow-up focusing on the right middle lobe.

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old woman. The patient has been experiencing an aggressive cough producing copious amounts of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum for about 11 years, with exacerbations similar to the current presentation today. Reports that the cough is worse in the morning and has had multiple evaluations in the past due to recurrent bouts of bronchitis requiring antibiotics treatment. The patient is a non-smoker.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Sarcoidosis with Lobar Bronchiectasis.

The clinical picture of a long-standing cough with thick, foamy sputum, morning predominance, and a restrictive spirometry pattern with focal right middle lobe opacities despite recurrent "bronchitis" strongly suggests sarcoidosis causing bronchiectasis, rather than simple chronic bronchitis or COPD. Given your history and imaging findings, do you have a history of skin lesions (like red bumps on the face or shins), eye pain/redness, or joint swelling?
